title: Kafka: Update messages to their latest versions
description:
Updates message parsing to support the latest versions of several message
types as defined by Kafka 3.7. Some of these type updates include Kafka
flexible versioning, which causes a significant layout change for some
message elements.

This doesn't add full support for all Kafka 3.7 messages but should cover
most of the common ones.

If you're going to do nothing if `api_version < 0`, then the packet needs to abort as malformed. Otherwise you end up not advancing the offset at all, and there's an infinite loop.

This introduced some possible infinite loops (there may have been some beforehand, but our fuzzing didn't detect it, and the fuzzed example in #19768 doesn't have an infinite loop before this commit.)

The problem is that some of these new messages don't advance the offset at all if the `api_version` is too low (especially an invalid number like below zero), presumably because that `api_version` doesn't have that message. Unfortunately, if there's fuzzed or erroneous data, not advancing the offset means an infinite loop. If there's any situation where the offset wouldn't be advanced, then you need to immediately abort dissection to avoid an infinite loop (and preferably add an expert info.)
This function now does not advance the offset at all if `api_version < 1`, leading to an infinite loop.

The existing code before this would add (bogus) elements when the api_version was too small for a message. That was bogus in that it was inconsistent with the version, yes, but it guaranteed that the offset advanced -- and of course it was always possible that the API version was where the bit error lay, instead of in the message.

The Kafka API version is a signed 16 bit integer; that's what the protocol says.

Of the two natural options: aborting a packet as soon as the API version is bogus (which includes any negative version), and adding an expert warning of the API version is too low for a message but minimally dissecting it according to the first version that could contain that message, I might choose the latter.

In addition to John's proposed fixes it probably wouldn't hurt to add an offset check to dissect_kafka_array_elements in order to guard against future regressions. In the fuzz capture in #19768, the array count is 443416832.

@EclipsedSolari, do you have time to take a look at this? Our fuzz testing job keeps creating issues for this.

Apologies for not seeing this until now.

I think I'd lean toward aborting the entire packet if the API version is negative. There are a couple of reasons for this.

First, Kafka messages new enough to support flexible versioning have tagged fields, which add at least 1 byte to message substructures even if the tagged fields are empty/unused. Older message versions may not have these and may read fields 1+ bytes offset from the expected locations as a result.

Second, some Kafka message structures have changed a lot between min version and max version. I don't necessarily expect everyone to be on the max version, but over time the average Kafka installation will drift farther from the min message format.

The combination of these factors means I'd expect parsing to generally fail if the API version isn't readable. Anecdotally, I put this MR together because I wasn't able to parse messages ~3-4 versions ahead of the Wireshark supported versions, so I doubt messages 10+ versions behind will do well. I'd rather fail consistently than make a best effort with potentially wrong or inconsistent results. But that gets into project philosophy, and I defer to your vision as long-term developers.

I'll work on creating a MR for the dissect_kafka_array_elements offset check. I see !15516 exists for assuming min API version (thank you John Thacker); please let me know if you'd like me to work on an alternate MR to abort the packet or if you'd like me to assist with the min API version work.
That is a reasonable point. Another option is to always use the maximum API version for negative versions, which might make more sense than the minimum version as this point.

Defaulting to max version does provide consistency with how the Kafka dissector currently handles messages with API versions greater than the max supported version; a message claiming to have version 1000 is probably not valid, but the message is implicitly parsed at max supported version anyway. "In case of invalid/unsupported API version, Wireshark defaults to the max supported version" is simple and consistent. I wasn't initially a fan, but the more I think about it, the more I like it.
